Abbreviation: NSA AC SR user
Name: 5G NSA Radio admission success ratio for NSA user
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of radio admitted NSA users.
Official Notes:
1. Request counter SGNB_NSA_ADMISSION_REQ is pegged along with SGNB_NSA_RAC_REJ_DUE_TO_NSA, SGNB_NSA_RAC_REJ_DUE_TO_NGBR and SGNB_CU_NSA_ADMISSION_UNSUCC.
2. In case of SGNB_NSA_RAC_REJ_DUE_TO_CPUE the failure is seen before admission control as the CP-UE is not able to take more UEs and hence it does not trigger other admission control counters.
3. SGNB_NSA_RAC_REJ_DUE_TO_CPUE counter is incremented also in handover use scenarios, while SGNB_NSA_ADMISSION_REQ nor SGNB_NSA_ADMISSION_SUCC are not.
Logical Formula: NSA AC SR user = 100 * NSA AC sucess / NSA AC sucess requests
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * Sum([Number of radio admitted UEs for NSA user]) /
Sum([Number of radio admission requests for NSA user] + [Number of admission rejects due to lack of CP-UE capacity for NSA user])

Abbreviation: UL resid BLER PUSCH
Name: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH
Description:
This KPI shows the residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PUSCH. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX HARQ retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions.
In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a different measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
Logical Formula:
100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (initial transmissions sent) =
100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (successful transmissions + transmissions failed after max retry)

Abbreviation: NSA IntergNB PSC chng prep SR tgNB
Name: 5G NSA Inter-gNB PSCell change preparation success ratio on target gNB
Description:
This KPI shows the inter-gNB PSCell change preparation success ratio measured in the target gNB. The preparation attempts are the number of X2AP: SGNB ADDITION REQUEST messages received from LTE eNB upon SN Change trigger. The successful preparations are given by the number of X2AP: SGNB ADDITION ACKNOWLEDGE sent by target gNB to LTE eNB, upon SN Change trigger.
Intra-frequency and inter-frequency PSCell changes are taken into account.
Logical Formula: IntergNB PSC chng prep att tgNB = Number of SGNB ADDITION REQUEST received from LTE eNB upon SN Change trigger
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * Sum([Number of outgoing SGNB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE sent to LTE eNB upon SN change trigger])
/
Sum([Number of incoming SGNB ADDITION REQUEST received from LTE eNB upon SN change trigger])

5GC2015 - For the scenarios where FDM activation is possible (2 layers) DL PDSCH throughput can be increased up to 11%, depending on the FDD frame configuration, MCS in use and additional DMRS activation.


[CB008227]
Scheduler needs to allocate additional resources in time and frequency to cell edge UEs. It will reduce the number of resources available for scheduling UEs with non-GBR traffic and experiencing better RF conditions. Feature will reduce overall cell throughput and spectral efficiency.

[CB006878]
KPI should be monitored as UL throughput can be improved with dynamic UL resource allocation, depending also on various factors as NRCELL.reqMinNumPuschPrb value and number of connected UEs. More PRBs can be utilized by a UE (on PUSCH) with CB006878, especially with low loaded cell (in terms of number of connected UEs).

[CB007219]
According to PR562529 solution, the gNB-DU can configure either native or alternative band of the P(S)Cell for the UE based on which band combination can provide higher throughput for the UE. With CB007219 enabled, the native band is selected for the P(S)Cell always when it is supported by the UE. This breaks PR562529 functionality and might result in selecting a non-optimal feature set for a non-CA UE, so the user might experience a drop in throughput comparing to the legacy solution. On the other hand, for the CA-capable UEs not supporting the native band of P(S)Cell/SCell(s), the peak throughput is expected to increase (due to utilization of additional spectrum from multiple carriers) depending on that which CA features are activated.

5GC002015 - For the scenarios where FDM activation is possible (2 layers) DL PDSCH throughput can be increased up to 11%, depending on the FDD frame configuration, MCS in use and additional DMRS activation.

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB006137]
This KPI is expected to decrease after setting NRCELL.increasePUSCHPrepTimeULCA to true on DL&UL TDD FR1 SCell candidates (done to increase their K2 value by 1 in order to support UL CA - CB006137 feature) in case there is no DL scheduling over TDD FR1 special slot (CB009007 PDSCH scheduling in special slot – FR1 TDD disabled) while one more PDCCH symbol is occupied in other DL data slots.

[CB010596]
When CB010596 is activated and some level of blocking is visible via NR_5739 and NR_5740 (see expert insights for these KPI as well), then this KPI should be monitored to ensure that the F1/F3 resource blocking is not causing DL performance degradation.

Newly introduced KPIs:

NR_5739a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
NR_5740a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F3 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F3 PDSCH allocation attempts

indicate blocking of allocation attempts of F1 and F3 HARQ A/N resources. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

Following counters are intended to monitor the level of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations:

M55308C00049 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F1 PUCCH
M55308C00050 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F3 PUCCH

Following KPIs should be monitored as well:

NR_5112d Average number of co-scheduled UEs in DL per data slot
NR_5088c 5G MAC PDU  Cell throughput on active PDSCH data slots on initial HARQ transmissions
[CB008927] Expected increase in case of full traffic, in case of mixed traffic (VoNR without robustness) and full traffic. Note (decrease side effect): In case of bursty traffic, the KPI may decrease due to lower PRBs utilization and no additional extra padding bits (because no RBG roundup).

[CB013945] The KPI may increase due to additional RBGs from dynamicswitch RAT0 allocation.

[CB012269] The feature goal is to mitigate inter-cell interference, which could improve overall system performance. However, gains are not guaranteed and depend on several factors and activated functionalities. Under some conditions, the loss of PRBs (physical resource blocks) excluded from transmission may not be regained by lower inter-cell interference.

[CB007491]
For high-speed UEs, an increase is expected due to better decoding performance. For low-speed UEs a decrease is expected due to additional DMRS overhead.

	
[CB014729] / [CNI-135068]
Risk of decrease as the rank is forced down at cell edge, more conservative DL LA for HO.

NetEng Comment:
UL THP is expectet to be lower with 5GC00938 introducing PRACH format 1. Single PRACH format 1 requires three consecutive UL slots therefore it's impacting UL performance.
In terms of CB006064 and CB007950, UL THP can be higher depending on wider channel bandwidths and with higher number of PRBs assigned to PUSCH or lower on narrower channel bandwidths and with lower setting of requested minimum PRBs for PUSCH, thus this KPI value should increase or decrease depending on the scenario.

5GC001118, CB007797 - Increased UL user peak rate due to higher modulation order. For cases where 256 QAM in PUSCH is activated (features 5GC001118/CB007797 is enabled) – UE UL peak rate can be increased and UL cell average throughput can be increase - cell level gain/loss depends mostly on the number of UEs in good radio conditions, which can use higher modulation – 256QAM.

5GC002396, CB008930 - when UE is using Full Tx Power in UL, and UE will use proper Tx antenna, it is expected that UL T-put will go up.

[CB006878]
KPI should be monitored as UL throughput can be improved with dynamic UL resource allocation, depending also on various factors as NRCELL.reqMinNumPuschPrb value and number of connected UEs. More PRBs can be utilized by a UE (on PUSCH) with CB006878, especially with low loaded cell (in terms of number of connected UEs).

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB012269] The feature goal is to mitigate inter-cell interference, which could improve overall system performance. However, gains are not guaranteed and depend on several factors and activated functionalities. Under some conditions, the loss of PRBs (physical resource blocks) excluded from transmission may not be regained by lower inter-cell interference.
	
[CB007491]
For high-speed UEs, an increase is expected due to better decoding performance. For low-speed UEs a decrease is expected due to additional DMRS overhead.

For 5GC001354 KPI is showing DL data throughput sent on PDCP level. Discarded DL PDCP SDUs are not counted. Duplicate DL PDCP PDUs are not counted. Retransmitted DL PDCP PDUs are not counted. As result with 5GC001354 where DL PDCP PDU retransmission, duplication and discarding are supported expected trend for this KPI is reduced DL data throughput. 

With CB009059 feature, thanks to the support of scheduling UM RLC non-GBR DRB DL data on SCells, the average DL throughput might increase in the SCell(s) and decrease in the PCell because of the data split. On the other hand, when CA is deconfigured due to the establishment of FR1 CA incompatible DRB, the average DL and UL throughputs decrease in the prior SCell(s) and might increase in the PCell (if the peak was not already reached). A similar impact is also expected due to the configuration of DRBs as not FR1 CA eligible.


[CB008227]
Scheduler needs to allocate additional resources in time and frequency to cell edge UEs. It will reduce the number of resources available for scheduling UEs with non-GBR traffic and experiencing better RF conditions. Feature will reduce overall cell throughput and spectral efficiency.

[CB007219]
According to PR562529 solution, the gNB-DU can configure either native or alternative band of the P(S)Cell for the UE based on which band combination can provide higher throughput for the UE. With CB007219 enabled, the native band is selected for the P(S)Cell always when it is supported by the UE. This breaks PR562529 functionality and might result in selecting a non-optimal feature set for a non-CA UE, so the user might experience a drop in throughput comparing to the legacy solution. On the other hand, for the CA-capable UEs not supporting the native band of P(S)Cell/SCell(s), the peak throughput is expected to increase (due to utilization of additional spectrum from multiple carriers) depending on that which CA features are activated.

In 5G19B implementation of counter ACC_UE_DL_DRB_DATA is changed as in below description:
"Before this change, UEs with DRB data buffered were checked and counted only when they had data buffered at the end of sample timer
(currently 20 slots). UEs that had buffered data only for a short period might have not been counted.
After change (PR495852) also UEs are included in counter if they had data buffered only for a few slots."
As counter values with this change will be higher it also directly impacts this KPI that will be lower. Noticed KPI change based on early 5G19B upgrade shows decrease from ~240 do 14Mbps

Later in 5G19B another modification takes place - counter ACC_UE_DL_DRB_DATA implementation is changed (1 slot interval) and it is being incremented per slot. It means that since that time (build ~.378) version A of this KPI shouldn't be used. Version B is proposed where additionally numerator is changed to include only user data (compared to current option where also dummy data is considered). Using verion A on soft after change will result in KPI values approx. 20 times lower.

[CB010596] when CB010596 is activated and some level of blocking is visible via NR_5739 and NR_5740 (see expert insights for these KPI as well), then this KPI should be monitored to ensure that the F1/F3 resource blocking is not causing DL performance degradation.

Newly introduced KPIs:

NR_5739a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
NR_5740a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F3 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F3 PDSCH allocation attempts

indicate blocking of allocation attempts of F1 and F3 HARQ A/N resources. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

Following counters are intended to monitor the level of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations:

M55308C00049 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F1 PUCCH
M55308C00050 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F3 PUCCH

Following KPIs should be monitored as well:

NR_5112d Average number of co-scheduled UEs in DL per data slot
NR_5088c 5G MAC PDU  Cell throughput on active PDSCH data slots on initial HARQ transmissions

NetEng Comment:
The impact (increase/decrease) of this KPI depends on traffic/mobility profile
If the UEs are stationary or the calls are short, then there will be less RRC reconfigurations to configure CA as the UEs that are outside SCell coverage are not configured with CA. For the UEs that are configured with CA the number of reconfigurations to add SCell is equal to that of blind SCell addition. In case of stationary UEs or very short calls there will be no A2 based SCell release triggered.
If the UEs are mobile and calls are long, then there will be more RRC reconfigurations to configure CA as SCell might be allocated and released multiple times based on changing radio conditions while UE moves within the PCell.

Abbreviation: PDCP SDU avg delay DL slice
Name: 5G SA PDCP SDU average delay in downlink per slice
Description: This KPI shows the downlink average delay for PDCP SDUs per slice, calculated as time difference between the reception of the PDCP SDU from NG-U and DL PDCP PDU is sent towards RLC layer.
Official Notes:
1. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: Sum PDCP SDU delay DL slice / Sum PDCP SDU pkt sent DL
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
Sum([DL PDCP SDU delay per slice per PLMN])
/
Sum([DL PDCP SDUs transmitted per slice per PLMN])

Abbreviation: PDCP SDU avg delay UL slice
Name: 5G SA PDCP SDU average delay in uplink per slice
Description: This KPI shows the uplink average delay for PDCP SDUs per slice, calculated as time difference between reception of UL PDCP PDU from RLC layer, and when the PDCP SDU is sent towards NG-U.
Official Notes:
1. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: Sum PDCP SDU delay UL slice / Sum PDCP SDU pkt rcvd UL
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
Sum([UL PDCP SDU delay per slice per PLMN])
/
Sum([UL PDCP SDUs received per slice per PLMN])

NetEng Comment:
This KPi is impacted every time when:
- there is no CCE available or not enough contiguous CCEs to apply selected AL, UEs are waiting for PDCCH resources allocation whereas free PDSCH resources are available in the cell (in certain BWP) and shared channels handles at least one initial transmission.
- CCE split activated, there is no free CCEs and the shared channel (PDSCH or PUSCH) handles only retransmission(s) that do not fulfill all available resources.

This KPI can be used for 5GC000791 feature verification. If activated, average number of CCE starvation shall decrease.

[CB009238]
The CB09238 NR-LTE DSS NR PDCCH load use for resource allocation feature, together with its LTE twin CB009237 LTE-NR DSS NR PDCCH load use for resource allocation feature, enhance Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS) by introducing NR PDCCH load considerations for resource allocation in LTE-NR  DSS scenarios. These features modify the Common Resource Manager (CRM) algorithm, incorporating the reported NR PDCCH load, alongside non-GBR and GBR load, as an additional factor in determining the optimal LTE and NR sharing ratio. This solution addresses scenarios where the reported NR PDCCH utilization exceeds the NR PDSCH or PUSCH utilization. That update should positively impact the starvation ratio.

[CB008927] If there are several PDSCH sub areas in the slot, the KPI PDCCH CCE starvation may slightly increase in RAT1 versus RAT0 because due to multiple subareas, max partial PRB's are allocated and UE maintains in CS1/CS2 list since the buffer is not completely drained out. The same KPI may decrease due to better Resource Management in small dedicated BWPs with RAT1 allocations.

Abbreviation: 5G SA acc SR
Name: 5G SA Accessibility success ratio
Description:
This KPI measures the end-to-end success rate of a user establishing a connection in 5G Standalone (SA) mode without considering the impact of RRC Inactive state. It is a comprehensive metric that evaluates the successful completion of multiple sequential connection procedures for the different variations of RRC Setup. These procedures include:
1) Radio Resource Control (RRC) Connection Setup: The success ratio of initial RRC setup requests across various service types, with exclusion of fallback procedures.
2) Initial UE Message Transmission: The success in sending the initial UE message to the 5G Core Network following a successful RRC connection. Both fallbacks due to re-establishment and resume procedure are included to properly maintain the value proportion between Initial UE Message and preceeding procedures.
3) Logical Connection Establishment: The success in establishing the higher-layer logical connection (e.g., PDU session) after initial core network communication.
4) UE Context Setup without resumption of context due to RRC Inactive state: The success in establishing the user's context at the gNB.
A higher KPI value indicates a more robust and efficient process for users to connect and access services within the 5G SA network.
Official Notes:
1. This Key Performance Indicator (KPI) quantifies User Equipment (UE) accessibility performance, distinct from Data Radio Bearer (DRB) establishment success.

2. Subsequent to the enablement of feature CB008225, it is recommended to monitor an alternative Key Performance Indicator (KPI) formula, designated NR_6262a, which accurately integrates Radio Resource Control (RRC) Resume events, thereby establishing a comprehensive accessibility metric.

3. This KPI is susceptible to degradation upon the activation of the Radio Resource Control (RRC) Inactive state functionality (feature CB008225). Specifically, the fourth component of the metric's computational expression will experience degradation, attributable to a substantial reduction in the initiation count of Initial Context Setup events.

4. Following to the activation of feature CB008225 the KPI value may be impacted by a reduction of overall RRC Setup attempts. This is because unsuccessful RRC Resume from RRC_INACTIVE prompts a transition to RRC_IDLE and subsequent RRC Setup. However, the population of UEs initiating RRC Setup will predominantly consist of those with poorer radio quality, as UEs with robust radio conditions would have successfully completed the RRC Resume procedure. Consequently, the first segment (RRC Setup related) of SR_InitialAccess of the NR_5151d formula is affected by missing RRCSetupComplete messages from these poor-quality UEs, and the fourth segment (Initial Context Setup procedure) of SR_InitialAccess is impacted by missing RRCReconfigurationComplete messages from the same group.
Logical Formula: SA access SR = 5G SA RRC connection establishment SR * 5G SA InitUeMessage SR * 5G SA NGAP connection establishment SR * 5G SA Initial context setup SR
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * (Sum([Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts that were completed successfully]) / Sum([Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Signaling] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Data] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Terminated Access] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Emergency] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for highPriorityAccess] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Voice Call] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated SMS] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Multimedia Priority Service] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mission Critical Service] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Video Calls]))
*
(Sum([Number of INITIAL UE MESSAGES sent]) / Sum([Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts that were completed successfully] + [Number of fallback RRCSetup successful as response to RRCReestablishmentReq] + [Number of successful RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup]))
*
(Sum([Initial UE message resulted in the establishment of UE-associated logical NG connection]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL UE MESSAGES sent]))
*
(Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE messages sent]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST messages received]))

[CB008227]
Scheduler needs to allocate additional resources in time and frequency to cell edge UEs. It will reduce the number of resources available for scheduling UEs with non-GBR traffic and experiencing better RF conditions. Feature will reduce overall cell throughput and spectral efficiency.

[CB006878]
KPI should be monitored as UL throughput can be improved with dynamic UL resource allocation, depending also on various factors as NRCELL.reqMinNumPuschPrb value and number of connected UEs. More PRBs can be utilized by a UE (on PUSCH) with CB006878, especially with low loaded cell (in terms of number of connected UEs).

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB010312]
UL cell throughput increase is expected when UL Overload Control is triggered in scenarios where PRB utilization is normally less than 100%. This feature  increases the scheduling of non-GBR UEs with high PF (Proportional Fair) metric which results in higher probability of utilizing PUSCH PRBs since it is expected that the higher the PF metric of the non-GBR UE, the higher is the probability of the UE having more data in its buffer. In rare cases, when the data rate of all UEs is quite low (e.g., ping UEs), a slight degradation is possible.

[CB008236]
Within a slot Aggregation bundle the repetitions are sent in consecutive uplink slots with identical PRB allocations. Each PRB allocation cause less resources for the other users. In such case the overall available PUSCH resources will be lower

NetEng Comment:
[CB008227]
Scheduler needs to allocate additional resources in time and frequency to cell edge UEs. It will reduce the number of resources available for scheduling UEs with non-GBR traffic and experiencing better RF conditions. Feature will reduce overall cell throughput and spectral efficiency.

[CB006878]
KPI should be monitored as UL throughput can be improved with dynamic UL resource allocation, depending also on various factors as NRCELL.reqMinNumPuschPrb value and number of connected UEs. More PRBs can be utilized by a UE (on PUSCH) with CB006878, especially with low loaded cell (in terms of number of connected UEs).

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB010312]
UL cell throughput increase is expected when UL Overload Control is triggered in scenarios where PRB utilization is normally less than 100%. This feature  increases the scheduling of non-GBR UEs with high PF (Proportional Fair) metric which results in higher probability of utilizing PUSCH PRBs since it is expected that the higher the PF metric of the non-GBR UE, the higher is the probability of the UE having more data in its buffer. In rare cases, when the data rate of all UEs is quite low (e.g., ping UEs), a slight degradation is possible.

[CB008236]
Within a slot Aggregation bundle the repetitions are sent in consecutive uplink slots with identical PRB allocations. Each PRB allocation cause less resources for the other users. In such case the overall available PUSCH resources will be lower

[CB008227]
Scheduler needs to allocate additional resources in time and frequency to cell edge UEs. It will reduce the number of resources available for scheduling UEs with non-GBR traffic and experiencing better RF conditions. Feature will reduce overall cell throughput and spectral efficiency.

[CB006878]
KPI should be monitored as UL throughput can be improved with dynamic UL resource allocation, depending also on various factors as NRCELL.reqMinNumPuschPrb value and number of connected UEs. More PRBs can be utilized by a UE (on PUSCH) with CB006878, especially with low loaded cell (in terms of number of connected UEs).

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB010312]
UL cell throughput increase is expected when UL Overload Control is triggered in scenarios where PRB utilization is normally less than 100%. This feature  increases the scheduling of non-GBR UEs with high PF (Proportional Fair) metric which results in higher probability of utilizing PUSCH PRBs since it is expected that the higher the PF metric of the non-GBR UE, the higher is the probability of the UE having more data in its buffer. In rare cases, when the data rate of all UEs is quite low (e.g., ping UEs), a slight degradation is possible.

[CB008236]
Within a slot Aggregation bundle the repetitions are sent in consecutive uplink slots with identical PRB allocations. Each PRB allocation cause less resources for the other users. In such case the overall available PUSCH resources will be lower

NetEng Comment:
[CB008227]
Scheduler needs to allocate additional resources in time and frequency to cell edge UEs. It will reduce the number of resources available for scheduling UEs with non-GBR traffic and experiencing better RF conditions. Feature will reduce overall cell throughput and spectral efficiency.

[CB009158] 
PRB pooling activation may impact the UE or cell throughput related KPIs.Depending on number of cells per L1 subpool and available PDSCH/PUSCH PRBs per L1 subpool, one or more cells in L1 subpool may support peak cell throughput simultaneously but not in all cells and/or slots. Therefore, it would be good to monitor throughput related KPIs.

[CB006878]
KPI should be monitored as UL throughput can be improved with dynamic UL resource allocation, depending also on various factors as NRCELL.reqMinNumPuschPrb value and number of connected UEs. More PRBs can be utilized by a UE (on PUSCH) with CB006878, especially with low loaded cell (in terms of number of connected UEs).

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB010596]
For some operators, when CB010596 is activated an improvement in NR_5259 KPI on cell level (5G Maximum MAC SDU Cell Throughput in UL on DTCH) may be noticed. It seems that it the case for low loaded networks. In networks with more traffic no improvement on cell level was noticed.

[CB007491]
For high-speed UEs, an increase is expected due to better decoding performance. For low-speed UEs a decrease is expected due to additional DMRS overhead.

[CB009238] Might be higher if it was limited due to PDCCH shortage. Max throughput might be visible in case of specific traffic (many small throughput UEs, without full buffer UEs).

Description: This KPI shows the average DL PDCP SDU end user throughput per DRB per QoS group 1. Abbreviation: SA % DL inact time VoNR
Name: 5G SA Percentage of DL inactivity time of VoNR calls
Description:
This KPI calculates percentage of DL inactivity time from all VoNR time.
Only inactivity times longer than 0.5 sec are considered.
Official Notes: The underlying inactivity time measurements comprising the numerator of this KPI are derived from u-plane counters, which are dynamically updated throughout the active call duration. This measurement methodology introduces a quantization uncertainty, contingent on the temporal granularity of the binning process, thereby compromising the real-time precision of the inactivity duration. Conversely, the c-plane counters, which constitute the denominator, are only incremented post-call termination, exhibiting a variable latency that can range from several seconds to multiple hours. This temporal misalignment in data aggregation can result in anomalously elevated KPI values during brief aggregation intervals. Therefore, monitoring this KPI is optimally performed on a daily basis rather than at 5- or 15-minute intervals, as the underlying call instance may persist beyond these shorter measurement periods, leading to potentially misleading instantaneous values.
Logical Formula:
100 * (Inact_time_i * dl_inact_vonr_bin_i)
/
(NG flow duration norm rel +  NG flow duration abnorm rel)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * Sum([Distribution of downlink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 01] * 0.75
+ [Distribution of downlink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 02] * 1.25
+ [Distribution of downlink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 03] * 1.75
+ [Distribution of downlink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 04] * 2.25

Abbreviation: SA QoS flow drop UserR
Name: 5G SA QoS Flow Drop Ratio - User view (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released QoS flow (5QI flows) attempts initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated).
Official Notes: It is valid for AMF when the NG_FLOW_REL_AMF_UE_LOST is triggered with respective number of QoS flow related to sending of UE Context Release Command to the source cell gNB in case of 'double Ng' scenario, when Radio Link Failure occurs during an ongoing QoS flow call and RRC Connection Re-establishment attempt fails on target or another cell. If then the UE does a new RRC Connection the QoS flow is set up during Initial Context Setup in the target or other cell. However, when AMF receives that service request with the Initial UE message through the target or other cell, it realizes that it already has the same UE Context but from the source cell (it has not been released yet as T-RLF is still running). In such case, AMF sends UE Context Release Command to the source cell. As the QoS flow has been successfully setup in the target or other cell, the QoS flow release in the source cell is not perceived as a drop (abnormal release) by the end user, as the service has been sustained with some interruption time and can't be considered as a drop in the QoS flow Drop Ratio from end user perspective. From network perspective it makes still sense to consider it as a drop to further optimize the network to reduce the interruption time to an acceptable value.
Logical Formula: SA QoS flow drop UserR = ((number of abnormally released QoS flow attempts initiated by gNB and AMF)/(Total number of QoS release attempts)) *100
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100*sum([Number of QoS flow IDs released for SA call] - [Number of QoS flow IDs released due to normal cause for SA call] - [Number of QoS Flows releases initiated by AMF for UE lost]) / sum([Number of QoS flow IDs released for SA call])

Abbreviation: 5G SA avg nr SA RRC conn usrs slct area
Name: 5G SA Average number of SA RRC connected users in selected area
Description:
This KPI shows the average number of RRC connected users in standalone operation.
KPI values are aggregated (summed) over the object dimension. Meaning that, if KPI is calculated over PLMN object, it shows the average number of users in all PLMN.
Official Notes:
1. The number of cells is calculated from measurement M55138 to ensure that only cells with SA enabled are counted.
2. SA users in RRC inactive state are included.
Logical Formula: SA Avg nr RRC connected UEs = (Cumulative sum of RRC connected users sampled / Number of samples) * Number of NRCells
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: (Sum([Average number of SA RRC users] + [Numerator for the average number of UEs in RRC_INACTIVE state]) / Sum([Average number of UEs denominator])) * Number_of_NRCEL
Time Summary Levels: Month; monthBH; week; weekBH; day; dayBH; hour; raw

Abbreviation: PDSCH alloc block to all F1
Name: 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
Description: This KPI shows the Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
Official Notes:
1. Applies to Long PUCCH
2. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The absolute level of allocation attempts blocking ratio indicated by this KPI may be high without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance). For reference the value of KPI before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that parameter pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.
Logical Formula: 5G PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 PUCCH to all PDSCH allocation attempts ratio = 100 * (Number of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 PUCCH resources) / (all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100 * Sum([Number of PDSCH allocations blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N resources]) / Sum([Number of PDSCH allocations blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N resources] + [Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F1 PUCCH])

NetEng Comment:
This KPI is used to monitor proper preregistration of CB010596 feature (i.e. setting these two parameters related to CB010596 feature: pucchF1ResOccConf and pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs). This KPI is not limited by CB010596 activation flag so it may be used from 23R4 to plan preregistration of the feature before its activation.

From NPI field test phase of the feature we can say that:

•	We do not have any evidence that F3 blocking (NR_5740) below 5% and F1 blocking below 0.5% (NR_5739) per day in average has any negative impact to DL cell or user throughput. 
For safety and precaution reason we do not advice to run with F1 blocking rate (NR_5739) above 1%, but we do not have any strong evidence that F1 blocking translate to DL performance degradation. It is advised to monitor cells/network if cells start running with F1 blocking than 1%.

•	We do not have any evidence that F3 blocking (NR_5740) below 25% and F1 blocking (NR_5739) below 1% per 15 min in average has any negative impact to DL cell or user throughput. 
For safety and precaution reason we do not advice to run with F1 blocking rate (NR_5739) above 1%, but we do not have any strong evidence that F1 blocking translate to DL performance degradation. It is advised to monitor cells/network if cells start running with F1 blocking than 1%.

Abbreviation: 5G SA RAN Pag SR
Name: 5G SA RAN Paging Success Ratio
Description: This KPI shows the Success Ratio for RAN Paging.
Official Notes:
1. This KPI includes only local gNB RAN paging for UEs in RRC_INACTIVE state (transfer of paging via Xn interface is not possible due to lack of mobility support in RRC_INACTIVE state in CB008225)

Abbreviation: 5G SA QoS Flow Stp SR excl EPS fback
Name: 5G SA QoS flow setup success ratio excluding EPS fallback
Description: This KPI shows the success ratio for QoS flow setup, excluding the cases when EPS fallback procedure is initiated.
Official Notes:
1. Only initial setups and incoming IRAT HO from LTE is considered. QoS Flow setups due to any other HO are excluded from this KPI.
2. CB008700 partial admission for Initial Context Setup is taken into consideration in this KPI. The possible ICSR causes for 22R3 release are: slice-not-supported-by-NG-RAN, handoverTargetNotAllowed, radioResourcesNotAvailable, releaseDueToNgRanGeneratedReason.
3. Unsuccessful RRC Resume from RRC_INACTIVE prompts a transition to RRC_IDLE and subsequent RRC Setup. Following CB008225 activation, this results in a reduction of overall RRC Setup attempts. However, the population of UEs initiating RRC Setup will predominantly consist of those with poorer radio quality, as UEs with robust radio conditions would have successfully completed the RRC Resume procedure. Consequently, the formula of this KPI is impacted by missing RRCReconfigurationComplete messages during Initial Context Setup procedure from these poor-quality UEs.
4. This Key Performance Indicator (KPI) is projected to degrade following the activation of the Radio Resource Control (RRC) Inactive state functionality (feature CB008225). This degradation is primarily attributable to a significant reduction in the initiation frequency of Initial Context Setup events.
5. New NR_6268a KPI is suggested to be monitored with CB008225 activated.
Logical Formula: 5G SA QoS Flow Setup SR excl EPS fallback = 100 * (QoS flow successful setups) / (QoS flow setup attempts - QoS flow setup attempts that initiated EPS fallback)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100 * Sum([Number of QoS Flow Setup Succ]) / Sum([Number of QoS Flow Setup attempts]-[Number of QoS Flows setup failures due to Fallback])

Description: This KPI shows the failure ratio for the last retry of HARQ transmission for PUSCH for VoNR per repetition bundle 4. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX HARQ retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions. In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a different measurement period than the initial transmission. Abbreviation: 5G SA QoS Flow Drop per con hour excl double-Ng
Name: 5G SA abnormal releases per connected hour (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
Description: This KPI shows the number of abnormally released QoS flows per hour of connected time excluding QoS flows releases initiated by AMF due to double-Ng.
Official Notes: It is valid for AMF when the NG_FLOW_REL_AMF_UE_LOST is triggered with respective number of QoS flow related to sending of UE Context Release Command to the source cell gNB in case of 'double Ng' scenario, when Radio Link Failure occurs during an ongoing QoS flow call and RRC Connection Re-establishment attempt fails on target or another cell. If then the UE does a new RRC Connection the QoS flow is set-up during Initial Context Setup in the target or other cell. However, when AMF receives that service request with the Initial UE message through the target or other cell, it realizes that it already has the same UE Context but from the source cell (it has not been released yet as T-RLF is still running). In such case, AMF sends UE Context Release Command to the source cell. As the QoS flow has been successfully setup in the target or other cell, the QoS flow release in the source cell is not perceived as a drop (abnormal release) by the end user, as the service has been sustained with some interruption time and can't be considered as a drop in the QoS flow Drop Ratio from end user perspective. From network perspective it makes still sense to consider it as a drop to further optimize the network to reduce the interruption time to an acceptable value.
Logical Formula: 5G SA QoS Flow Drop per con hour excl double-Ng = (1000 * 3600)*(number of abnormally released QoS flow attempts initiated by gNB and AMF - Number of QosFlows releases initiated by AMF due to double-Ng)/(In-session connected time for QoS flows)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: (1000*3600*sum([Number of QoS flow IDs released for SA call] - [Number of QoS flow IDs released due to normal cause for SA call] - [Number of QoS Flows releases initiated by AMF for UE lost]) / sum([In-session connected time for QoS flows]))

Abbreviation: Avg delay DL air-if AM RLC per cell
Name: 5G Average delay DL air-interface for AM RLC per cell
Description:
This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) time it takes for AM DL RLC SDU packet to travel from gNB-DU to UE, and back from the UE to DU.
 The exact time span is measured as the difference between: 
- the point in time when an RLC SDU packet is sent to UE from gNB-DU
- the point in time when the reception of RLC ACK for AM mode for the corresponding RLC SDU packet is confirmed in DU in the same component.
Official Notes:
1. Compliance with 3GPP requirement from TS 28.552 chapter 5.1.1.1.1, as 3GPP states 'RLC SDU part arriving at MAC layer' rather than 'RLC ACK for AM mode for the corresponding RLC SDU packet is confirmed in DU in the same component'.
2. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
3. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: sum of (delay DL air-interface for AM RLC per cell) / (total number of RLC SDUs transmitted to UE successfully)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([AM RLC SDU with polling bit DL delay]) / (1000*sum([Number of successfully transmitted AM RLC SDUs with polling bit in DL]))

Abbreviation: Avg delay DL CU-UP per cell
Name: 5G Average delay DL in CU-UP per cell
Description: This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) PDCP SDU delay on the downlink within the gNB-CU-UP per cell, for all PDCP packets.
Official Notes:
1. Data forwarding is not counted over Xn nor NG interfaces.
2. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
3. 3GPP requirement from TS 28.552 chapter 5.1.3.3.1.
4. Discarded and duplicated PDCP SDUs are not counted.
5. When CB009189 Service-aware Scheduling Request and H-ArQ retransmissions feature is enabled, value of this KPI will decrease.
6. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: Sum of (time when sending a PDCP SDU to the gNB-DU at the egress PDCP layer on F1-U/Xn-U, minus time of arrival of the same packet at NG-U ingress IP termination) / (total number of PDCP SDUs arriving at NG-U ingress IP termination)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([DL PDCP SDU delay in CU UP]) / (1000*sum([Number of DL PDCP SDUs sent to gNB-DU over F1U/XnU/X2U]))

Abbreviation: Avg DL sched delay MAC UE DRX act time of DRX Cycle per cell
Name: 5G Average DL scheduling delay in MAC with UE in DRX with active time of DRX Cycle per cell
Description: This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) MAC scheduling delay in the downlink within L2-PS while the UE monitors the PDCCH. The UE monitors the PDCCH if it is configured without DRX or when it is configured with DRX and the DRX Cycle is within active time. DRX Cycle consists of active and sleep time, where active time means that UE monitors PDCCH, while sleep time means that UE neither performs any monitoring on PDCCH nor any reporting on PUCCH. DRX inactive phase is when UE monitors PDCCH and is equal to active time of DRX Cycle.
Official Notes:
1. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
2. Counter's name DL_INIT_SCHD_DLY_DRX_ACT is purely related to DRX inactive phase, but the DRX_ACT abbreviation is related to DRX active time of DRX Cycle.
3. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: sum of DL initial scheduling delay when UE is in DRX with active time of DRX Cycle / number of samples
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([DL initial scheduling delay - DRX ACTIVE]) / (1000*sum([DL initial scheduling delay - DRX ACTIVE denominator]))

Abbreviation: 5G Average GTP-U packet delay in DL over F1-U per cell
Name: 5G Average GTP-U packet delay in DL over F1-U per cell
Description:
This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) time it takes for GTP-U packet in DL to travel over F1-U interface, per cell. 
The exact time span is divided by two and is measured as a difference between:
- sending the GTP-U packet to the gNB-DU at the GTP ingress termination (sending the PDCP packet from PDCP - DUD),
- receiving feedback from the gNB-DU at the egress GTP termination (feedback receiving point at the PDCP SN - DDDS),
with exclusion of processing time in gNB-DU.
Official Notes:
1. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
2. This KPI is 3GPP compliant with 5.1.3.3.2 of 28.552 for Average delay DL on F1-U.
3. This KPI is applicable only for Cloud Deployments.
4. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: sum of (DL GTP packet delay over F1-U) / (Number of DL GTP packets)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([DL GTP packet delay over F1-U]) / (1000*sum([Number of DL GTP packets]))

Abbreviation: 5G Average air-interface UM RLC SDU delay in DL per cell
Name: 5G Average air-interface UM RLC SDU delay in DL per cell
Description:
This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) time it takes for RLC SDU packet to travel from DU to the UE and back from the UE to DU, in the downlink direction for UM RLC per cell. 
The exact time span is measured as difference between:
- RLC SDU packet arrives in MAC layer and
- the reception of HARQ ACK for UM mode for the corresponding RLC SDU packet at air interface.
Official Notes:
1. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
2. This KPI is 3GPP compliant with 5.1.1.1.1 of 28.552 for Average delay DL air-interface with HARQ ACK for UM.
3. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: sum of (delay DL air-interface for UM RLC per cell) / (total number of RLC SDUs transmitted to UE successfully)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([DL RLC UM Air interface delay]) / (1000*sum([Number of DL UM RLC SDUs sent to UE successfully]))

Abbreviation: SA QoS flow DR cell
Name: 5G SA QoS flow drop ratio per cell
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released QoS flows initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of QoS flow releases (gNB and AMF initiated), including the releases due to Intra-NR successful handover.
Official Notes:
1. This formula is intended to be calculated at NRCEL level.
2. The same call can trigger multiple times the counter NG_FLOW_REL_IANR_SUC_HO in several cells in case of successful Intra-NR Handovers, so the use of the KPI on gNB or network level is not advised.
3. The counters NG_FLOW_REL and NG_FLOW_REL_NORMAL are not incremented in case of successful Intra-NR HO.
4. The PM counter NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE, treated as normal release type, is added into denominator to reduce the impact on increased drop ratio KPI value due to activation of CB008225 feature for RRC Inactive state transitions.
Logical Formula:
SA QoS flow drop R per cell =  100 * (All QoS flow releases - normal Qos flow releases)
/
 (All QoS flow releases + Number of successful Intra-NR HO QoS flow releases + Number of suspended QoS flows)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100 *  Sum([Number of QoS flow IDs released for SA call] - [Number of QoS flow IDs released due to normal cause for SA call]) / Sum([Number of QoS flow IDs released for SA call] + [Number of QoS Flows released due to successful Intra NR HO at source cell] + [Number of QoS Flows suspended during RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_INACTIVE state transition])
Formula Notes: 1. The PM counter NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE is added into denominator to reduce the impact on increased drop ratio KPI value due to activation of CB008225 feature for RRC Inactive state transitions. In numerator only abnormal release types should be counted, while in denominator all release types should be counted, and this is the reason why NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE must be added into denominator, which should be treated as normal release type. In the past it was decided that NG_FLOW_REL counter shall not be incremented in case QoS Flow is released during its RRC Inactive state is maintained.

Abbreviation: SA QoS flow drop UserR
Name: 5G SA QoS Flow Drop Ratio - User view (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released QoS flow (5QI flows) attempts initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated).
Official Notes:
1. It is valid for AMF when the NG_FLOW_REL_AMF_UE_LOST is triggered with respective number of QoS flow related to sending of UE Context Release Command to the source cell gNB in case of 'double Ng' scenario, when Radio Link Failure occurs during an ongoing QoS flow call and RRC Connection Re-establishment attempt fails on target or another cell. If then the UE does a new RRC Connection the QoS flow is set up during Initial Context Setup in the target or other cell. However, when AMF receives that service request with the Initial UE message through the target or other cell, it realizes that it already has the same UE Context but from the source cell (it has not been released yet as T-RLF is still running). In such case, AMF sends UE Context Release Command to the source cell. As the QoS flow has been successfully setup in the target or other cell, the QoS flow release in the source cell is not perceived as a drop (abnormal release) by the end user, as the service has been sustained with some interruption time and can't be considered as a drop in the QoS flow Drop Ratio from end user perspective. From network perspective it makes still sense to consider it as a drop to further optimize the network to reduce the interruption time to an acceptable value.
2. The PM counter NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE, treated as normal release type, is added into denominator to reduce the impact on increased drop ratio KPI value due to activation of CB008225 feature for RRC Inactive state transitions.

Abbreviation: 5G SA acc SR
Name: 5G SA Accessibility success ratio
Description:
This KPI measures the end-to-end success rate of a user establishing a connection in 5G Standalone (SA) mode. It is a comprehensive metric that evaluates the successful completion of multiple sequential stages of the connection procedure. These stages include:
1) Radio Resource Control (RRC) Connection Setup and Resume: The success rate of initial RRC setup requests and RRC resumes across various service types.
2) Initial UE Message Transmission: The success in sending the initial UE message to the 5G Core Network following a successful RRC connection.
3) Logical Connection Establishment: The success in establishing the higher-layer logical connection (e.g., PDU session) after initial core network communication.
4) UE Context Setup and resumption: The success in establishing or resuming (if it has been put on hold) the user's context at the gNB.
A higher KPI value indicates a more robust and efficient process for users to connect and access services within the 5G SA network.
Official Notes:
1. This KPI measures UE accessibility, not DRB-related success.
2. The first segment now includes RRC Resume fallback events (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_SUCC) to accurately capture all RRC setup attempts. These addresses previously uncounted failures during RRC Resume fallback (e.g., after an RNA update with CB008225 activated).
3. The fourth component now incorporates RRC Resume events (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST1, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST) that lead to UE Context resumption, while subtracting events (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT, NRRCC_RRC_REL_WITH_SUSP_RNAU) that do not. This adjustment accounts for RRC Resume attempts that result in service re-establishment without incrementing Initial Context Setup (ICS) counters.
4. RRC re-establishment procedures (RRC_REESTAB_FALLBACK, REESTAB_ACC_FALLBACK) are excluded from the first segment as this KPI focuses on new call establishments. However, REESTAB_ACC_FALLBACK is included in the second segment because it triggers NNGCC_INIT_UE_MSG_SENT.
5. Unsuccessful RRC Resume from RRC_INACTIVE prompts a fallback to RRC_IDLE and subsequent RRC Setup. Following CB008225 activation, this results in a reduction of overall RRC Setup attempts. However, the population of UEs initiating RRC Setup will predominantly consist of those with poorer radio quality, as UEs with robust radio conditions would have successfully completed the RRC Resume procedure. Consequently, the first segment of the NR_5151d formula is affected by missing RRCSetupComplete messages from these poor-quality UEs, and the fourth segment is impacted by missing RRCReconfigurationComplete messages from the same group.
Logical Formula: SA access SR = 5G SA RRC connection establishment SR (including fallback) * 5G SA InitUeMessage SR * 5G SA NGAP connection establishment SR * 5G SA Initial context setup SR (including context resumption due to RRC Resume)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * (Sum([Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts that were completed successfully] + [Number of successful RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup]) / Sum([Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Signaling] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Data] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Terminated Access] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Emergency] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for highPriorityAccess] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Voice Call] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated SMS] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Multimedia Priority Service] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mission Critical Service] + [Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts for Mobile Originated Video Calls] + [Number of RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup attempts]))
*
(Sum([Number of INITIAL UE MESSAGES sent]) / Sum([Number of RRC CONNECTION Attempts that were completed successfully] + [Number of fallback RRCSetup successful as response to RRCReestablishmentReq] + [Number of successful RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup]))
*
(Sum([Initial UE message resulted in the establishment of UE-associated logical NG connection]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL UE MESSAGES sent]))
*
(Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE messages sent] + [Number of RRC Resume Successes at gNB-CU]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST messages received] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests1 received at gNB-CU] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests received at gNB-CU] - [Number of RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup attempts] - [RRC releases with suspension sent from gNB-CU in response to RRC Resume Request for RNA update]))

Abbreviation: SA compl acc SR
Name: 5G SA Complete Accessibility success ratio
Description:
This Key Performance Indicator (KPI) quantifies the end-to-end successful connection establishment probability for User Equipment (UE) operating in 5G Standalone (SA) mode. It serves as a holistic metric, assessing the successful execution of a sequential process, which is partitioned into two distinct phases, each assigned a specific weighting factor.

The initial phase encompasses:
- Radio Resource Control (RRC) Connection Setup and Resume Fallback: The successful completion probability of initial RRC connection establishment attempts and RRC resume procedures necessitating fallback, across diverse service categories.
- Initial UE Message Transmission: The successful transmission of the initial Non-Access Stratum (NAS) message to the 5G Core Network, subsequent to successful RRC connection establishment.
- Logical Connection Establishment: The successful establishment of the higher-layer logical bearer (e.g., Protocol Data Unit (PDU) session) subsequent to initial core network signaling exchange.
- UE Context Setup: The successful establishment of the UE context within the gNodeB (gNB).

The second phase is defined by the RRC Resume procedure, specifically encompassing events associated with Radio Network Area (RNA) Update procedures (facilitating UE location reporting without requiring NG interface resource re-establishment), while explicitly excluding instances involving RRC Resume fallback.

An elevated KPI value signifies enhanced robustness and operational efficiency for UE connectivity and service access within the 5G Standalone (SA) network architecture.
Official Notes:
1. The weighting factors employed for each success ratio are mutually exclusive, signifying that they are derived from and applied to distinct, non-overlapping sets of underlying events.
2. This KPI measures UE accessibility, not DRB-related success.
3. The first segment (RRC Setup related) of SR_InitialAccess includes RRC Resume fallback events (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_SUCC) to accurately capture all RRC setup attempts. These addresses uncounted failures during RRC Resume fallback (e.g., after an RNA update with CB008225 activated) in other KPI formula NR_5151d.
4. RRC re-establishment procedures (RRC_REESTAB_FALLBACK, REESTAB_ACC_FALLBACK) are excluded from the first segment (RRC Setup related) of SR_InitialAccess as this KPI focuses on new call establishments. However, REESTAB_ACC_FALLBACK is included in the second segment (Initial UE Message to RRC Setup ratio) because it triggers NNGCC_INIT_UE_MSG_SENT.
5. Unsuccessful RRC Resume from RRC_INACTIVE prompts a transition to RRC_IDLE and subsequent RRC Setup. Following CB008225 activation, this results in a reduction of overall RRC Setup attempts. However, the population of UEs initiating RRC Setup will predominantly consist of those with poorer radio quality, as UEs with robust radio conditions would have successfully completed the RRC Resume procedure. Consequently, the first segment (RRC Setup related) of SR_InitialAccess of the NR_6262a formula is affected by missing RRCSetupComplete messages from these poor-quality UEs, and the fourth segment (Initial Context Setup procedure) of SR_InitialAccess is impacted by missing RRCReconfigurationComplete messages from the same group.

Abbreviation: Resid BLER DL
Name: 5G Residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH
Description:
This KPI shows the residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX HARQ retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions.
In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a different measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
HARQ feedback DTX is considered as unsuccessful.
Official Notes: If speculative DTX algorithm is activated, algorithm will treat DTX in HARQ feedback as ACK (MAC CE are excluded) under good RF condition.
Logical Formula: Resid BLER DL = 100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (successful transmissions + transmissions failed after max retry)

The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

Abbreviation: 5G SA Combined Ctx Est Resume Perf Index
Name: 5G SA Combined Context Establishment & Resume Performance Index
Description: This KPI measures a combined performance index for successful UE context establishment (transition from RRC Idle to RRC Connected) and RRC resume procedures (transition from RRC Inactive to RRC Connected) in 5G Standalone (SA) mode. It calculates a weighted sum of the individual success ratios for initial context setup and RRC resume. Each success ratio is weighted by the proportion of its successful count relative to the total adjusted attempts for both procedures. Attempts that resulted in RRC resume fallback to RRC Setup or RRC release with suspension for RNA update are excluded from the total adjusted attempts, providing a more accurate measure of the gNB's ability to successfully handle these transitions. This KPI offers a comprehensive view of the network's performance in managing UE RRC states.
Official Notes:
1. Comprehensive RRC State Transition Coverage:
NR_5168a Limitation: NR_5168a focuses only on the initial context setup procedure (typically from RRC Idle to RRC Connected). It does not account for other crucial UE state transitions, particularly from RRC Inactive to RRC Connected.
New KPI Improvement: The new KPI significantly enhances coverage by explicitly including RRC resume procedures (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST1, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST, and NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC). This is vital for modern 5G SA networks where the RRC Inactive state is extensively used for power saving and faster service access. By covering both Idle-to-Connected and Inactive-to-Connected transitions, the new KPI provides a more complete picture of UE context management.

2. Refined Attempt Denominator for RRC Resume:
NR_5168a Irrelevance: NR_5168a does not deal with RRC resume attempts.
New KPI Improvement: The denominator for RRC resume attempts (AdjustedRRCResumeAttempts) is more accurate. It subtracts NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT (attempts that fall back to RRC Setup) and NRRCC_RRC_REL_WITH_SUSP_RNAU (RRC Releases with suspension for RNA update). This refinement ensures that the success rate is calculated against actual resume attempts that the gNB was expected to handle directly, excluding those that were designed to transition differently (e.g., fallbacks) or were terminated for specific reasons.

3. Holistic Performance Index: 
The new KPI is structured as a "Performance Index" rather than a simple success ratio. It calculates a weighted sum of the individual success ratios (for initial setup and resume), where each ratio is weighted by the proportion of its successful count relative to the TotalAdjustedAttempts. This complex weighting scheme provides a more nuanced and potentially insightful measure of overall context management performance, reflecting not just individual success rates but also their contribution to the aggregated successful transitions. This offers a more holistic and realistic view of the network's ability to bring UEs into an active RRC Connected state.
Logical Formula:
100 * (SuccessfulInitialContextSetups / InitialContextRequests) * (SuccessfulInitialContextSetups / TotalAdjustedAttempts) + 100 * (SuccessfulRRCResumes / AdjustedRRCResumeAttempts) * (SuccessfulRRCResumes / TotalAdjustedAttempts)

where:
InitialContextRequests = Sum([NNGCC_UE_CTXT_STP_REQ_RECD])
SuccessfulInitialContextSetups = Sum([NNGCC_UE_CTXT_STP_RESP_SENT])
RRCResumeRequests = Sum([NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST1]) + Sum([NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST])
SuccessfulRRCResumes = Sum([NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC])
RRCResumeFallbackAttempts = Sum([NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT])
RRCResumeReleaseSuspension = Sum([NRRCC_RRC_REL_WITH_SUSP_RNAU])
AdjustedRRCResumeAttempts = RRCResumeRequests - RRCResumeFallbackAttempts - RRCResumeReleaseSuspension
TotalAdjustedAttempts = InitialContextRequests + AdjustedRRCResumeAttempts
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * ((Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE messages sent]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST messages received]))
* (Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE messages sent]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST messages received] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests1 received at gNB-CU] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests received at gNB-CU] - [Number of RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup attempts] - [RRC releases with suspension sent from gNB-CU in response to RRC Resume Request for RNA update]))
+ 
 (Sum([Number of RRC Resume Successes at gNB-CU]) / Sum([Number of RRC Resume Requests1 received at gNB-CU] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests received at gNB-CU] - [Number of RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup attempts] - [RRC releases with suspension sent from gNB-CU in response to RRC Resume Request for RNA update]))
* 
 (Sum([Number of RRC Resume Successes at gNB-CU]) / Sum([Number of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST messages received] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests1 received at gNB-CU] + [Number of RRC Resume Requests received at gNB-CU] - [Number of RRC connection resume fallbacks to RRC Setup attempts] - [RRC releases with suspension sent from gNB-CU in response to RRC Resume Request for RNA update])))

[5GC001745] In release 5G21B in DSS cells with feature 5GC001745 enabled, the code rate was incorrectly computed in slots #0/5 due to rate matching around LTE signals, this has resulted in too high MCS, negatively impacting DL BLER. With PR593840 this should be fixed and DL BLER should decrease starting from build SBTS21B_ENB_0000_000187_000000

[5GC001745] PR607701 - There was issue in early 5G21B builds, with 5GC001745 enabled, which could result in this KPI degrading. This is fixed in 5G21B and onwards starting with SBTS21B_ENB_0000_001197_000000 SW.

[5GC002574] PR630845 - There was issue in early 22R1 builds, with 5GC002574enabled, which could result in this KPI degrading. This is fixed in 22R1 and onwards starting with SBTS22R2_ENB_0000_000378_000000 SW.

Starting from 22R2 NRBTS.NRCELL.actSpeculativeDtx is used to treat
DTX in HARQ feedback as ACK in good RF condition. Backporting in
21A/21B/22R1 is possible through NRCELL.tmpParam7

In 23R2, this KPI might increase due to automatically applied "DRX Status Synchronization Algorithm Change in U-Plane" which improves the DRX status synchronization between CA P(S)Cell and SCell(s).

[CB011031] Decrease expected after CB011031 activation if CB011031 is correctly configured (5G SSB to overlap in time and frequency domain with LTE PBCH).

[CB012269] This feature aims to mitigate inter-cell interference and provide better channel estimation. Lower BLER is expected in the TRS slots, which can improve achieved throughput.

[CB008927] Expected slight increase due to small PDSCH grants (1 to 3 PRBs)- it is side effect of activation the CB008927 feature

[CB013742] decrease intended after feature activation

[CB007491] KPI may be impacted, The impact is unknown as MCS can also change due to LA.

Abbreviation: UL resid BLER PUSCH
Name: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH
Description:
This KPI shows the residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PUSCH. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX harq retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions.
In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a diferent measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
Logical Formula:
100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (initial transmissions sent) =
100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (successful transmissions + transmissions failed after max retry)
