NetEng Comment:
5GC002015 - For the scenarios where FDM activation is possible (2 layers) DL PDSCH throughput can be increased up to 11%, depending on the FDD frame configuration, MCS in use and additional DMRS activation.

[CB008985]
The assumption is that the use case where one supercell has the same coverage as set of several normal cells is considered.
Comparing one supercell to set of several normal cells covering the same area (the assumption is that same RRU type is used in both normal cells and supercells), average cell throughput per coverage area may change.
- Assuming that as ‘before case’ we would take the sum of KPI from all normal cells (to consider traffic load to whole area covered by supercell) and compare it to one supercell, Cell Throughput will decrease.

[CB006137]
This KPI is expected to decrease after setting NRCELL.increasePUSCHPrepTimeULCA to true on DL&UL TDD FR1 SCell candidates (done to increase their K2 value by 1 in order to support UL CA - CB006137 feature) in case there is no DL scheduling over TDD FR1 special slot (CB009007 PDSCH scheduling in special slot – FR1 TDD disabled) while one more PDCCH symbol is occupied in other DL data slots.

[CB010596]
When CB010596 is activated and some level of blocking is visible via NR_5739 and NR_5740 (see expert insights for these KPI as well), then this KPI should be monitored to ensure that the F1/F3 resource blocking is not causing DL performance degradation.

Newly introduced KPIs:

NR_5739a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
NR_5740a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F3 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F3 PDSCH allocation attempts

indicate blocking of allocation attempts of F1 and F3 HARQ A/N resources. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

Following counters are intended to monitor the level of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations:

M55308C00049 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F1 PUCCH
M55308C00050 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F3 PUCCH

Following KPIs should be monitored as well:

NR_5112d Average number of co-scheduled UEs in DL per data slot
NR_5088c 5G MAC PDU  Cell throughput on active PDSCH data slots on initial HARQ transmissions
[CB008927] Expected increase in case of full traffic, in case of mixed traffic (VoNR without robustness) and full traffic. Note (decrease side effect): In case of bursty traffic, the KPI may decrease due to lower PRBs utilization and no additional extra padding bits (because no RBG roundup).

[CB013945] The KPI may increase due to additional RBGs from dynamicswitch RAT0 allocation.

[CB012269] The feature goal is to mitigate inter-cell interference, which could improve overall system performance. However, gains are not guaranteed and depend on several factors and activated functionalities. Under some conditions, the loss of PRBs (physical resource blocks) excluded from transmission may not be regained by lower inter-cell interference.

[CB007491]
For high-speed UEs, an increase is expected due to better decoding performance. For low-speed UEs a decrease is expected due to additional DMRS overhead.

	
[CB014729] / [CNI-135068]
Risk of decrease as the rank is forced down at cell edge, more conservative DL LA for HO.

In 5G19B implementation of counter ACC_UE_DL_DRB_DATA is changed as in below description:
"Before this change, UEs with DRB data buffered were checked and counted only when they had data buffered at the end of sample timer
(currently 20 slots). UEs that had buffered data only for a short period might have not been counted.
After change (PR495852) also UEs are included in counter if they had data buffered only for a few slots."
As counter values with this change will be higher it also directly impacts this KPI that will be lower. Noticed KPI change based on early 5G19B upgrade shows decrease from ~240 do 14Mbps

Later in 5G19B another modification takes place - counter ACC_UE_DL_DRB_DATA implementation is changed (1 slot interval) and it is being incremented per slot. It means that since that time (build ~.378) version A of this KPI shouldn't be used. Version B is proposed where additionally numerator is changed to include only user data (compared to current option where also dummy data is considered). Using verion A on soft after change will result in KPI values approx. 20 times lower.

KPI (counter) keeps track of new calls (within measurement period) only. As a result its value can not be comparable to average number of NSA users (NR_5124) especially with long calls (which exceeds measurement period).

In terms of CB006064, CB007950, CB007827 and CB007449 maximum number of RRC connected UEs is expected to be higher, especially if configuration includes maximum possible CSI and SR periodicity, wider channel bandwidths and lower minimum number of PRBs allocated to the PUSCH (at the expense of allocation of these PRBs to PUCCH).

[CB007219]
With this feature, more UEs might be configured with CA. Per each CA UE, more periodic channel state information reporting (pCSI) resources are assigned comparing to a non-CA UE, while both UEs share the same pCSI pool. Therefore, the more CA UEs in the cell, the lower the cell capacity is.

[CB007491]
Decrease is possible due to PUCCH additional DMRS, but only for some configurations. To be checked with the PUCCH_Configuration tool.

[CB014729] / [CNI-135068]
An increase is expected as the rank is forced down at the cell edge and more conservative DL LA for HO is applied. This may decrease the RRM resources used.

Abbreviation: SA 5QI1 QoS flow DR cell
Name: 5G SA 5QI1 QoS flow drop ratio per cell
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released 5QI1 QoS flows initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of 5QI1 QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated), including the releases due to Intra-NR successful handover.
Official Notes:
1. This formula is intended to be calculated at NRCEL level.
2. The same call can trigger multiple times the counter NG_FLOW_REL_IANR_SUC_HO_5QI1 in several cells in case of successful Intra-NR Handovers, so the use of the KPI on gNB or network level is not advised.
3. The counters NG_FLOW_REL_ABNORMAL_5QI1 and NG_FLOW_REL_NORMAL_5QI1 are not incremented in case of successful Intra-NR HO.
Logical Formula:
SA 5QI1 QoS flow drop R per cell =  100 * (number of abnormally released 5QI1 QoS flows initiated by gNB and AMF)
/
 (Number of Normal 5QI1 QoS releases + Number of Abnormal 5QI1 QoS releases + Number of successful Intra-NR HO QoS flow releases)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * Sum([Number of 5QI-1 QoS flows released due to abnormal causes])
/
Sum([Number of 5QI-1 QoS Flows releases considered to be Normal release] + [Number of 5QI-1 QoS flows released due to abnormal causes] + [Number of 5QI-1 QoS Flows released due to successful Intra NR HO at source cell])

This KPI allows to measure CA throughput from PCell perspective on PDCP level.

[CB007219]
According to PR562529 solution, the gNB-DU can configure either native or alternative band of the P(S)Cell for the UE based on which band combination can provide higher throughput for the UE. Abbreviation: SA 5QI1 QoS flow drop UserR
Name: 5G SA 5QI1 QoS Flow Drop Ratio - User view (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released 5QI1 QoS flow attempts initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of 5QI1 QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated).
Official Notes: It is valid for AMF when the NG_FLOW_REL_AMF_UE_LOST_5QI1 is triggered with respective number of 5QI1 QoS flow related to sending of UE Context Release Command to the source cell gNB in case of 'double Ng' scenario, when Radio Link Failure occurs during an ongoing 5QI1 QoS flow call and RRC Connection Re-establishment attempt fails on target or another cell. If then the UE does a new RRC Connection the 5QI1 QoS flow is set up during Initial Context Setup in the target or other cell. However, when AMF receives that service request with the Initial UE message through the target or other cell, it realizes that it already has the same UE Context but from the source cell (it has not been released yet as T-RLF is still running). In such case, AMF sends UE Context Release Command to the source cell. As the 5QI1 QoS flow has been successfully setup in the target or other cell, the 5QI1 QoS flow release in the source cell is not perceived as a drop (abnormal release) by the end user, as the service has been sustained with some interruption time and can't be considered as a drop in the 5QI1 QoS flow Drop Ratio from end user perspective. From network perspective it makes still sense to consider it as a drop to further optimize the network to reduce the interruption time to an acceptable value.
Logical Formula: SA 5QI1 QoS flow drop UserR = ((number of abnormally released 5QI1 QoS flow attempts initiated by gNB and AMF)/(Total number of 5QI1 QoS release attempts)) *100
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100*sum([Number of 5QI-1 QoS flows released due to abnormal causes]-[Number of 5QI-1 QoS Flows releases initiated by AMF for UE lost]) / sum([Number of 5QI-1 QoS Flows releases considered to be Normal release] + [Number of 5QI-1 QoS flows released due to abnormal causes])
Time Summary Levels: Month; monthBH; week; weekBH; day; dayBH; hour; raw

Abbreviation: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH for VoNR
Name: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH for VoNR
Description: This KPI shows the failure ratio for the last retry of HARQ transmission for PUSCH for VoNR. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX HARQ retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions. In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a different measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
Logical Formula: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH for VoNR = 100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (successful transmissions + transmissions failed after max retry)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100*sum([UL 5QI1 SDUs not received by gNB after maximum HARQ retransmissions]) / sum([Successful PUSCH any transmissions with 5QI1 data] + [UL 5QI1 SDUs not received by gNB after maximum HARQ retransmissions])

Abbreviation: 5G Average air-interface MAC SDU delay in UL per cell
Name: 5G Average air-interface MAC SDU delay in UL per cell
Description:
This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) time it takes for MAC SDU packet to travel from the UE to the DU from the point of time when UL grant is assigned, per cell. 
The exact time span is measured as difference between:
- the UL MAC SDU is scheduled in MAC layer as per the scheduling grant sent to UE and
- the UL MAC SDU is successfully sent to RLC.
Official Notes:
1. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
2. This KPI is 3GPP compliant with 5.1.1.1.3 of 28.552 for Average delay UL air-interface.
3. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: sum of (delay UL air-interface for MAC SDU per cell) / (total number of UL MAC SDUs is sent to RLC)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([UL Packet Air interface delay]) / (1000*sum([Number of UL MAC SDUs sent to RLC layer]))

Official Notes:
1. Request counters are incremented after gNB has selected the best band combination for the given user, which is done at after admission control. Abbreviation: 5G SA Normal gNB-init rel ratio - RAN view
Name: 5G SA Normal gNB-initiated release ratio - RAN view
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of normal releases, due to inactivity, redirection, preemption, serving cell load reduction, UE not reachable in RRC_INACTIVE state and due to UE preference with UAI, initiated by gNB, compared to all releases, for SA access.
Official Notes:
1. The following counter SA_UE_CTX_REL_PREEM is for cause "Release due to preemption" and shall be treated as abnormal release from user perspective but normal release from RAN view.
2. The following counter SA_UE_CTX_REL_PREEM_REDIR is for cause "Redirection" and shall be considered within NRRCC_RRC_RELEASE_REDIR_NR and NRRCC_RRC_RELEASE_REDIR_LTE and does not need to be added into numerator of the formula.

Abbreviation: 5G SA NG Flow Stp SR
Name: 5G SA NG Flow Setup Success Ratio (QoS Flow Aligned)
Description: This KPI measures a combined performance index for successful NG Flow Setup (initiated from RRC Idle to RRC Connected) and NG Flow Setup triggered by RRC resume procedures (transition from RRC Inactive to RRC Connected) in 5G Standalone (SA) mode. It calculates a weighted sum of the individual success ratios for initial NG Flow Setup and NG Flow Setup triggered by RRC resume. Crucially, all attempts and successes are normalized to represent the number of QoS Flow events. Attempts that resulted in RRC resume fallback to RRC Setup or RRC release with suspension for RNA update are excluded from the adjusted RRC resume attempts, and these adjusted RRC resume attempts are then converted to an estimated number of QoS Flow attempts. This provides a more accurate and consistently-unitized measure of the gNB's ability to successfully handle these transitions and establish user plane flows across various UE RRC states.
Official Notes:
1. Comprehensive RRC State Transition Coverage:
Original NR_5776a Limitation: The original NR_5776a primarily focuses on initial NG Flow Setup attempts. While it includes an adjustment for fallback attempts, it does not explicitly account for NG Flow Setup procedures that occur as a direct consequence of RRC resume (i.e., transitions from RRC Inactive to RRC Connected that then trigger an NG Flow Setup).
New KPI Improvement: The new KPI significantly enhances coverage by explicitly linking NG Flow Setup success to RRC resume procedures (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST1, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST, and NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC). This is crucial for modern 5G SA networks where the RRC Inactive state is extensively used for power saving and faster service access, and subsequent NG Flow Setups are often triggered upon successful RRC resume. By covering both initial and resume-driven NG Flow Setups, it provides a more complete picture of the network's ability to establish user plane flows efficiently across different RRC state transitions.

2. Refined Attempt Denominator for RRC Resume:
Original NR_5776a Irrelevance: The original NR_5776a formula does not consider RRC resume attempts, thus lacking the necessary refinement for these scenarios.
New KPI Improvement: The denominator for RRC resume attempts is made more accurate by subtracting NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT (attempts that fall back to RRC Setup) and NRRCC_RRC_REL_WITH_SUSP_RNAU (RRC Releases with suspension for RNA update). This ensures that the success rate is calculated against actual RRC resume attempts that were expected to lead to an NG Flow Setup directly, excluding those designed to transition differently or terminated for specific reasons.

3. Holistic Performance Index:
The new KPI is structured as a "Performance Index" rather than a simple success ratio. It calculates a weighted sum of the individual success ratios (for initial NG Flow Setup and RRC resume leading to NG Flow Setup), where each ratio is weighted by the proportion of its successful count relative to the Expanded Total Attempts (initial NG Flow Setup attempts plus adjusted RRC resume attempts). This complex weighting scheme provides a more nuanced and potentially insightful measure of overall NG Flow Setup performance, reflecting not just individual success rates but also their contribution to the aggregated successful flow establishments. This offers a more holistic and realistic view of the network's ability to set up user plane flows for UEs transitioning through various RRC states.
Logical Formula:
100 * ((Initial NG Flow Setup Success Rate) * (Adjusted Initial NG Flow Setup Attempts / Total Estimated QoS Flow Attempts) 
     + (Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Setup Success Rate) * (Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Setup Attempts / Total Estimated QoS Flow Attempts))
Where:

Initial NG Flow Setup Success Rate: Sum(NG_FLOW_SETUP_SUCC) / Sum(Adjusted Initial NG Flow Setup Attempts)

Adjusted Initial NG Flow Setup Attempts = (NG_FLOW_SETUP_ATT_TOT - NG_FLOW_SETUP_FAIL_FALLBACK) (This part remains largely the same, assuming NG_FLOW_SETUP_ATT_TOT and NG_FLOW_SETUP_SUCC are already QoS Flow counts)
Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Setup Success Rate: Sum(Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Successes) / Sum(Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Setup Attempts)

Adjusted RRC Resume Procedures = (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST1 + NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST - NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT - NRRCC_RRC_REL_WITH_SUSP_RNAU)
Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Setup Attempts = Adjusted RRC Resume Procedures * Average_QoS_Flows_per_RRC_Resume
Estimated RRC Resume NG Flow Successes = NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC * Average_QoS_Flows_per_RRC_Resume (Here, Average_QoS_Flows_per_RRC_Resume is a crucial estimation factor. This could be a configurable parameter, a network-wide average, or derived from other counters if available, e.g., Sum([NG_FLOW_RESUME_RRC_INACT_CONN]) / Sum([NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC]) if such specific counters exist.)

NetEng Comment:
The 5G RACH procedure is not only used to set up the initial connection. Also handover, beam recovery and re-synchronization when leaving DRX state use the RACH procedure. Sometimes, the number of RACH procedures for the initial connection setup is only a minor part of the total number of RACH procedures. This means that NR_5022a in practice covers both accessibility and retainability issues, and there is no easy way to separate these by PM counters.//

From live network analysis (5G19A 3.7TD), it looks like if dlDataSplitMode is set to "dlOverF1U", and there is a RACH failure, then this somehow is interpreted as a user plane problem and NX2CC_UE_RELEASE_ABNORMAL will be incremented instead of rlf_initiated_ue_rach_fail or rlf_initiated_ue_scg_chge_fail. In such network configurations, the NX2CC_UE_RELEASE_ABNORMAL should probably be included in the denominator of this KPI.//

Formula does not work if there is standalone (SA) traffic in the cell: SA traffic increments ra_msg3_recep but not rlf_initiated_ue_rach_fail and rlf_initiated_ue_scg_chge_fail

Abbreviation: Resid BLER DL
Name: 5G Residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH
Description:
This KPI shows the residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX harq retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions.
In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a diferent measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
HARQ feedback DTX is considered as unsuccessful.
Official Notes: If speculative DTX algorithm is activated, algorithm will treat DTX in HARQ feedback as ACK (MAC CE are excluded) under good RF condition.
Logical Formula: Resid BLER DL 256QAM tab = 100*(Number of unsuccessful DL TB transmissions)/ (Total number of initial DL TB transmissions)

NetEng Comment:
[5GC001745] In release 5G21B in DSS cells with feature 5GC001745 enabled, the code rate was incorrectly computed in slots #0/5 due to rate matching around LTE signals, this has resulted in too high MCS, negatively impacting DL BLER. With PR593840 this should be fixed and DL BLER should decrease starting from build SBTS21B_ENB_0000_000187_000000

Starting from 22R2 NRBTS.NRCELL.actSpeculativeDtx is used to treat
DTX in HARQ feedback as ACK in good RF condition. Backporting in
21A/21B/22R1 is possible through NRCELL.tmpParam7

[CB008662] from 23R1 (version b) covers reserved MCS introduced with CB008662 for adaptive retransmission

[CB011031] Decrease expected after CB011031 activation if CB011031 is correctly configured (5G SSB to overlap in time and frequency domain with LTE PBCH).
[CB008927] Expected slight increase due to small PDSCH grants (1 to 3 PRBs)- it is side effect of activation the CB008927 feature

[CB012269] Feature aim to mitigate inter-cell interference and provide better channel estimation. That can lead improve the spectral efficiency and keep the residual BLER low.

[CB007491] KPI may be impacted, The impact is unknown as MCS can also change due to LA.

[CB014729] / [CNI-135068]
Decrease intended as PDSCH BLER at cell edge should improve.

Abbreviation: UL resid BLER PUSCH
Name: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH
Description:
This KPI shows the residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PUSCH. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX harq retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions.
In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a diferent measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
Logical Formula:
100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (initial transmissions sent) =
100 * (transmissions failed after max retry) / (successful transmissions + transmissions failed after max retry)

[CB010596]
When CB010596 is activated and some level of blocking is visible via NR_5739 and NR_5740 (see expert insights for these KPI as well), then this KPI should be monitored to ensure that the F1/F3 resource blocking is not causing DL performance degradation.

Newly introduced KPIs:

NR_5740a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F3 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F3 PDSCH allocation attempts

indicate blocking of allocation attempts of F1 and F3 HARQ A/N resources. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

NetEng Comment:
[CB010596] when CB010596 is activated and some level of blocking is visible via NR_5739 and NR_5740 (see expert insights for these KPI as well), then this KPI should be monitored to ensure that the F1/F3 resource blocking is not causing DL performance degradation.

Newly introduced KPIs:

NR_5739a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
NR_5740a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F3 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F3 PDSCH allocation attempts

indicate blocking of allocation attempts of F1 and F3 HARQ A/N resources. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

Following counters are intended to monitor the level of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations:

M55308C00049 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F1 PUCCH
M55308C00050 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F3 PUCCH

Following KPIs should be monitored as well:

NR_5112d Average number of co-scheduled UEs in DL per data slot
NR_5088c 5G MAC PDU  Cell throughput on active PDSCH data slots on initial HARQ transmissions

NetEng Comment:
This KPI allows to measure CA throughput from PCell perspective on PDCP level.

[CB007219]
According to PR562529 solution, the gNB-DU can configure either native or alternative band of the P(S)Cell for the UE based on which band combination can provide higher throughput for the UE. With CB007219 enabled, the native band is selected for the P(S)Cell always when it is supported by the UE. This breaks PR562529 functionality and might result in selecting a non-optimal feature set for a non-CA UE, so the user might experience a drop in throughput comparing to the legacy solution. On the other hand, for the CA-capable UEs not supporting the native band of P(S)Cell/SCell(s), the peak throughput is expected to increase (due to utilization of additional spectrum from multiple carriers) depending on that which CA features are activated.

This KPI allows to measure CA throughput from PCell perspective on PDCP level.

[CB007219]
According to PR562529 solution, the gNB-DU can configure either native or alternative band of the P(S)Cell for the UE based on which band combination can provide higher throughput for the UE. With CB007219 enabled, the native band is selected for the P(S)Cell always when it is supported by the UE. This breaks PR562529 functionality and might result in selecting a non-optimal feature set for a non-CA UE, so the user might experience a drop in throughput comparing to the legacy solution. On the other hand, for the CA-capable UEs not supporting the native band of P(S)Cell/SCell(s), the peak throughput is expected to increase (due to utilization of additional spectrum from multiple carriers) depending on that which CA features are activated.

Abbreviation: Avg nr sched UE DL
Name: 5G Average number of scheduled UEs in DL
Description: This KPI shows the average number of scheduled UEs per downlink slots.
Logical Formula: Avg nr sched UE DL = Number of sheduled UEs / number of DL slots
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: Sum([Total Number of co-scheduled UEs on PDSCH]) / Sum([Sum of DL Data slots])
Time Summary Levels: Month; monthBH; week; weekBH; day; dayBH; hour; raw
NetEng Comment:
[CB010596] when CB010596 is activated and some level of blocking is visible via NR_5739 and NR_5740 (see expert insights for these KPI as well), then this KPI should be monitored to ensure that the F1/F3 resource blocking is not causing DL performance degradation.

Newly introduced KPIs:

NR_5739a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F1 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F1 PDSCH allocation attempts
NR_5740a 5G Ratio of PDSCH allocation attempts blocked due to lack of F3 HARQ A/N PUCCH resources to all F3 PDSCH allocation attempts

indicate blocking of allocation attempts of F1 and F3 HARQ A/N resources. With many UEs in the cell a blocked resource for a specific UE may be used by another UE. The UE that could have been scheduled on 3 or 4 downlink slots and is blocked for F3 PUCCH resources for HARQ AN will use the F1 resource so that 2 of the 4 downlink slots can be scheduled and the UE will wait up to two downlink slots for additional downlink allocations. The absolute level of blocking indicated by this KPI may be high especially for NR_5740a without negative impact on cell level (i.e. number of successful allocations in the cell will be still high and there will be no impact on PDSCH performance).

For reference the value of both KPIs before the activation of CB010596 should be considered, and only an increase on top of such reference level and simultaneous decrease of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations and number of UEs scheduled per DL slot may indicate that pucchNumberHarqAnPrbs is set too low and may impact PDSCH performance.

Following counters are intended to monitor the level of successful HARQ A/N resource allocations:

M55308C00049 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F1 PUCCH
M55308C00050 Number of successful PDSCH allocations that require HARQ feedback on F3 PUCCH

Following KPIs should be monitored as well:

NR_5112d Average number of co-scheduled UEs in DL per data slot
NR_5088c 5G MAC PDU  Cell throughput on active PDSCH data slots on initial HARQ transmissions

Abbreviation: SA % UL inact time VoNR
Name: 5G SA Percentage of UL inactivity time of VoNR calls
Description:
This KPI calculates percentage of UL inactivity time from all VoNR time.
Only inactivity times longer than 0.5 sec are considered.
Official Notes: The underlying inactivity time measurements comprising the numerator of this KPI are derived from u-plane counters, which are dynamically updated throughout the active call duration. This measurement methodology introduces a quantization uncertainty, contingent on the temporal granularity of the binning process, thereby compromising the real-time precision of the inactivity duration. Conversely, the c-plane counters, which constitute the denominator, are only incremented post-call termination, exhibiting a variable latency that can range from several seconds to multiple hours. This temporal misalignment in data aggregation can result in anomalously elevated KPI values during brief aggregation intervals. Therefore, monitoring this KPI is optimally performed on a daily basis rather than at 5- or 15-minute intervals, as the underlying call instance may persist beyond these shorter measurement periods, leading to potentially misleading instantaneous values.
Logical Formula:
100 * (Inact_time_i * ul_inact_vonr_bin_i)
/
(NG flow duration norm rel +  NG flow duration abnorm rel)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name:
100 * Sum([Distribution of uplink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 01] * 0.75
+ [Distribution of uplink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 02] * 1.25
+ [Distribution of uplink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 03] * 1.75
+ [Distribution of uplink inactivity for VoNR - Bin 04] * 2.25

/
(Sum([In-session connected time for 5QI1 QoS flows released due to normal cause] + [In-session connected time for 5QI1 QoS flows released due to abnormal cause]) / 1000)

Abbreviation: 5G Residual BLER PUSCH VoNR repetition bundle 1 (no repetition)
Name: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH for VoNR per repetition bundle 1 (no repetition)
Description: This KPI shows the failure ratio for the last retry of HARQ transmission for PUSCH for VoNR per repetition bundle 1 (no repetition). Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX HARQ retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions. In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a different measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
Official Notes:
1. Related to DFT-s-OFDM only.
2. It considers transmissions with 64QAM MCS.
Logical Formula: 5G Residual BLER in PUSCH for VoNR per repetition bundle 1 (no repetition) = 100 * (transmissions failed after max retry for bundle rep1) / (successful transmissions for bundle rep1 + transmissions failed after max retry for bundle rep1)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: 100*sum([Unsuccessful PUSCH transmissions by last HARQ reTx with DFT-s-OFDM and 64QAM table for slot agg rep1]) / sum([Successful PUSCH transmissions by any Tx with DFT-s-OFDM and 64QAM table for slot agg rep1] + [Unsuccessful PUSCH transmissions by last HARQ reTx with DFT-s-OFDM and 64QAM table for slot agg rep1])
Time Summary Levels: Raw, Hourly, Daily, Weekly

Abbreviation: Avg PDCP re-ord delay UL per cell
Name: 5G Average PDCP re-ordering delay in the UL per cell
Description: This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) PDCP re-ordering delay on the uplink within the gNB-CU-UP per cell.
Official Notes:
1. 3GPP requirement from TS 28.552 chapter 5.1.1.1.5.
2. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
3. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: Sum of (time when sending a PDCP SDU to the core at the egress PDCP layer on NG-U IP termination, minus time of arrival of the same packet at F1-U/Xn-U ingress) / (total number of PDCP SDUs leaving the NG-U egress)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([UL PDCP SDU delay in CU UP]) / (1000*sum([UL PDCP SDUs sent to upper SAP]))

1. Request counters are incremented after gNB has selected the best band combination for the given user, which is done at after admission control. Abbreviation: 5G Average gNB-DU burst RLC SDU delay in DL per cell
Name: 5G Average gNB-DU burst RLC SDU delay in DL per cell
Description:
This KPI provides the average (arithmetic mean) time it takes for Initial RLC SDU packet in a burst to travel from gNB-DU to UE, per cell.
The exact time span is measured as difference between:
- the RLC SDU is received at DU and 
- the first RLC SDU transmitted on the air interface.
Official Notes:
1. Delay counter is in microseconds, thus the division by 1000 is required to get millisecond value.
2. This KPI is 3GPP compliant with 5.1.3.4.2 of 28.552 for internal L2 (DU) DL processing delay per burst.
3. The PM counter within the KPI is reported with a 1 microsecond resolution, which significantly exceeds its practical measurement precision (aligned with the 3GPP standard's 100 microseconds requirement).
Fluctuations below 100 microseconds should be considered measurement noise. Furthermore, even shifts exceeding 100 microseconds in delay may not uniformly translate to performance degradation across all dependent QoS KPIs. The severity and perceptibility of impact are critically influenced by the transmission type, application sensitivity, and the prevailing radio channel quality. Therefore, the effective degradation threshold can range from a 200 microseconds shift for certain transmissions to 1 ms or even tens of milliseconds for others before becoming significant.
Logical Formula: sum of (INIT RLC SDU in burst DL IP latency in DU) / (Number of init RLC SDU in burst transmitted)
Summarisation Formula with NE Name: sum([INIT RLC SDU in burst DL IP latency in DU]) / (1000*sum([Number of init RLC SDU in burst transmitted]))

Abbreviation: SA Active QoS flow drop Ratio excl double-Ng
Name: 5G SA Active QoS Flow Drop Ratio (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
Description: This KPI shows the ratio of QoS flows with data in a buffer that were abnormally released excluding active QoS flow releases initiated by AMF due to double-Ng to the total number of QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated).
Official Notes: 1. The PM counter NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE, treated as normal release type, is added into denominator to reduce the impact on increased drop ratio KPI value due to activation of CB008225 feature for RRC Inactive state transitions.

Summarisation Formula with NE Name: (100 * Sum([Number of in-session QoS flows released due to abnormal causes] - [Number of in-session QoS Flow releases initiated by AMF for UE lost])/Sum([Number of QoS flow IDs released for SA call] + [Number of QoS Flows suspended during RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_INACTIVE state transition]))
Formula Notes: 1. The PM counter NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE is added into denominator to reduce the impact on increased drop ratio KPI value due to activation of CB008225 feature for RRC Inactive state transitions. In numerator only abnormal release types should be counted, while in denominator all release types should be counted, and this is the reason why NG_FLOW_SUSP_RRC_CONN_INACTIVE must be added into denominator, which should be treated as normal release type. In the past it was decided that NG_FLOW_REL counter shall not be incremented in case QoS Flow is released during its RRC Inactive state is maintained. Moreover, for this KPI the denominator counts all release types regardless of data session activity.

Abbreviation: 5G SA Log Conn Est SR
Name: 5G SA Logical Connection Establishment Success Ratio
Description: This KPI measures a combined performance index for successful logical connection establishment (transition from RRC Idle to RRC Connected) and logical connection re-establishment via RRC resume procedures (transition from RRC Inactive to RRC Connected) in 5G Standalone (SA) mode. It calculates a weighted sum of the individual success ratios for initial logical connection setup and RRC resume leading to logical connection. Each success ratio is weighted by the proportion of its successful count relative to the total adjusted attempts for both procedures. Attempts that resulted in RRC resume fallback to RRC Setup or RRC release with suspension for RNA update are excluded from the total adjusted attempts, providing a more accurate measure of the gNB's ability to successfully handle these transitions. This KPI offers a comprehensive view of the network's performance in managing UE logical connection states.
Official Notes:
1. Comprehensive RRC State Transition Coverage:
Original NR_6227a Limitation: The original NR_6227a focuses solely on the initial logical connection establishment procedure, typically initiated from an RRC Idle state. It does not account for other crucial UE state transitions that lead to logical connection establishment, particularly those originating from an RRC Inactive state.
New KPI Improvement: The new KPI significantly enhances coverage by explicitly integrating the success of logical connection establishments that follow RRC resume procedures (NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST1, NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_REQUEST, and NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_SUCC). This is vital for modern 5G SA networks where the RRC Inactive state is extensively utilized for power saving and faster service access. By covering both initial and resume-driven logical connection establishments, the new KPI provides a more complete and realistic picture of the network's user plane connectivity performance.

2. Refined Attempt Denominator for RRC Resume:
Original NR_6227a Irrelevance: The original NR_6227a formula does not consider RRC resume attempts, thus lacking the necessary refinement for these scenarios.
New KPI Improvement: The denominator for RRC resume attempts is made more accurate by subtracting NRRCC_RRC_RESUME_FALLBACK_ATT (attempts that fall back to RRC Setup) and NRRCC_RRC_REL_WITH_SUSP_RNAU (RRC Releases with suspension for RNA update). This refinement ensures that the success rate is calculated against actual RRC resume attempts that the gNB was expected to handle directly for logical connection re-establishment, excluding those that were designed to transition differently (e.g., fallbacks) or were terminated for specific reasons.

3. Holistic Performance Index:
The new KPI is structured as a "Performance Index" rather than a simple success ratio. It calculates a weighted sum of the individual success ratios (for initial logical connection establishment and RRC resume leading to logical connection), where each ratio is weighted by the proportion of its successful count relative to the Expanded Total Attempts (initial logical connection attempts plus adjusted RRC resume attempts). This complex weighting scheme provides a more nuanced and potentially insightful measure of overall user plane logical connection performance, reflecting not just individual success rates but also their contribution to the aggregated successful connections. This offers a more holistic and realistic view of the network's ability to provide user plane connectivity to UEs transitioning through various RRC states.

Description: This KPI shows the ratio of normal releases, due to inactivity, redirection, preemption, serving cell load reduction and due to UE preference with UAI, initiated by gNB, compared to all releases, for SA access.
Official Notes:
1. The following counter SA_UE_CTX_REL_PREEM is for cause "Release due to preemption" and shall be treated as abnormal release from user perspective but normal release from RAN view.
2. The following counter SA_UE_CTX_REL_PREEM_REDIR is for cause "Redirection" and shall be considered within NRRCC_RRC_RELEASE_REDIR_NR and NRRCC_RRC_RELEASE_REDIR_LTE and does not need to be added into numerator of the formula.
3. The following counter INACT_UE_CTXT_REL_RED_LOAD is for cause "Reduce load in serving cell" and shall be treated as abnormal release from user perspective but normal release from RAN view.
4. During RRC Release with 'redirection' there may happen a race condition concurrency between NGAP: UE Context Release Command initiated by AMF and NGAP: UE Context Release Request initiated by gNB. Both counters NRRCC_RRC_RELEASE_REDIR_LTE and NRRCC_RRC_RELEASE_REDIR_NR may be updated, but NNGCC_UE_CTXT_REL_REQ_SENT will not be updated because NGAP: UE Context Release Command initiated by AMF has been received before the gNB had the chance to initiate the release by itself.
Logical Formula: SA Norm gNB init rel R = 100 * (Release Request due to Inactive + releases due to redirection + releases due to preemption + releases due to UE preference with UE Assisted Information + releases due to serving cell load reduction) / (Rel Request sent)
